patients.summary: Retired construction foreman with COPD, hypertension and hyperlipidemia who joined the practice in late 2024. Acute acalculous cholecystitis in September 2025 treated without surgery; in March 2026 a long ICU stay for ARDS with tracheostomy, a second acalculous cholecystitis drained percutaneously, rehab, and home by June. Not seen in the office since October 2025; post-hospital visit booked.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
67 yo retired construction foreman, new to us. Had been seeing a doctor in another town for years and wants someone closer to home in Florence. Signed release for the old office's records today.

Main issue is COPD. Prior office called it GOLD Group C; he does not have his spirometry with him. Uses tiotropium capsule every morning and the fluticasone/salmeterol disk morning and night. Albuterol a couple times a week, mostly carrying things up stairs or in cold air. Gets winded on a long flight of stairs but walks his usual loop around the neighborhood fine. No hospitalizations for breathing that he can recall. No cough with blood, no fevers.

BP on lisinopril 10 for years, no side effects. Atorvastatin 40 and aspirin 81 for cholesterol, started by the prior doctor.

PMH: COPD, HTN, hyperlipidemia.
PSH: appendix out at 14. Left inguinal hernia repaired at 61.
Meds: tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily; fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 one inhalation twice daily; albuterol 90 mcg 1-2 puffs q4-6h prn; lisinopril 10 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: sulfa drugs, rash.
FH: father had a heart attack at 68. Mother had COPD. Brother had an ischemic stroke at 66.
SH: smoked for decades, about 48 pack-years, quit in 2023 and has stayed off. A drink or two a week, social. Divorced, lives alone. Spent his career running crews on commercial jobs.

Exam: well appearing, talking in full sentences. Lungs with mildly diminished air movement throughout, no wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular, no murmur. No edema. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed RLQ and left groin scars.

A/P
1. COPD, stable on LAMA plus ICS/LABA. Inhaler technique reviewed, capsule device done correctly. Continue.
2. HTN, controlled today. Continue lisinopril 10.
3. Hyperlipidemia. Continue atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81. CMP, CBC, lipids drawn.
4. Lung cancer screening: qualifies on pack-years and quit date. Low-dose CT ordered.
5. High-dose flu and updated COVID given. RSV vaccine at a nurse visit next month. Pneumococcal and shingles to sort out once old records are in.
Return for Medicare wellness visit in the winter.

documents.title: Your blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Robert, kidney and liver numbers are normal, blood count normal, and the cholesterol is where it should be on the atorvastatin. Nothing to change. The CT scheduling office will call you about the lung screening scan.

events.reason: Records from prior primary care office

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records received by fax from the patient's previous primary care office, covering several years of visits.

Problem list on their summary: COPD (GOLD Group C), hypertension, hyperlipidemia. Former tobacco use.
Medications: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 twice daily, albuterol as needed, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergy: sulfa (rash).
Screening: colonoscopy 2018, no polyps, repeat interval 10 years.
No spirometry report included in the packet.

Scanned to the chart. PCP reviewed; lists match what he gave us.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for RSV vaccine per PCP plan (age plus COPD). Screening questions negative, no prior RSV dose. Arexvy given L deltoid, lot recorded. Waited 15 min, no reaction. VIS given.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Indication: annual lung cancer screening, 67-year-old former smoker, 48 pack-years, quit 2023. Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast. Findings: no pulmonary nodules. Airways patent. No consolidation or effusion. Heart size normal, no pericardial effusion. No enlarged mediastinal or hilar lymph nodes. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Low-Dose CT Lung Screening
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Outpatient imaging center report. Low-dose chest CT for lung cancer screening. No nodules. Lung-RADS 1. Recommend repeat screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Lung screening scan
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news on the CT, no spots on the lungs at all. We repeat this once a year, so next one around January. See you in February for the wellness visit.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. Feels about the same as in the fall, breathing steady through the winter so far, albuterol maybe twice a week. No falls. Independent in all ADLs and IADLs, drives, does his own shopping. Hearing fine in the room. Sleeps ok.

Screens: PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2. No safety concerns at home. Advance directive: does not have one, took the packet home.

Prevention review:
- Colonoscopy 2018 normal at prior office, next 2028.
- Lung CT January, Lung-RADS 1. Next due January.
- Hep C never checked, drawn today.
- AAA screen: male, former smoker, never done. Ultrasound ordered.
- Pneumococcal: no record of any dose. PCV20 today.
- Shingrix dose 1 today, dose 2 at May visit.
- RSV done in December. Flu and COVID done in November.

Vitals as charted. Lungs with distant breath sounds, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema.

COPD, HTN, lipids all stable on current regimen. No changes. Follow-up in about 3 months.

documents.title: Hepatitis C test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hep C screen came back negative. That one never needs repeating unless something changes. The vascular lab should be calling about the aorta ultrasound.

reports.text: Screening ultrasound of the abdominal aorta. The aorta is visualized from the diaphragm to the bifurcation. Maximal anteroposterior diameter of the infrarenal aorta measured outer wall to outer wall is within normal limits. No aneurysm. Common iliac arteries normal caliber where seen.
reports.conclusion: No abdominal aortic aneurysm. No further screening needed.

documents.title: AAA Screening Ultrasound
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Screening aortic ultrasound: normal caliber aorta, no aneurysm. One-time screen complete. Reviewed by PCP, result released to patient.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request for tiotropium capsules and fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50. Prior office's prescriptions ran out. Sent under PCP with 90-day supply and 3 refills each. Patient aware via voicemail.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine check. Breathing good this spring, had the windows open, no flares. Rescue inhaler once or twice a week. Taking everything. Felt a little achy for a day after the first Shingrix.

O: vitals as charted. Lungs diminished at bases equally, no wheeze or crackles. RRR. Ext no edema.

A/P: COPD stable. HTN controlled. Shingrix #2 today, series done. BMP on lisinopril. RTC fall with flu shot.

documents.title: Albuterol
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can I get a new albuterol sent over, the one in the truck is almost empty and the other one expired. Same pharmacy.

documents.title: RE: Albuterol
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sent two inhalers so you can keep one in the truck. Let us know if you find you're using it more than a few times a week.

events.reason: Fever and right upper quadrant pain

reports.text: Indication: fever, right upper quadrant pain. The gallbladder is distended with a thickened wall and pericholecystic fluid. No gallstones or sludge-layering stones are seen. Common bile duct is normal in caliber. Liver normal in size and echotexture without focal lesion. Right kidney unremarkable. Pancreas head unremarkable where seen.
reports.conclusion: Gallbladder wall thickening, distension and pericholecystic fluid without gallstones, consistent with acute acalculous cholecystitis.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, visit date 9/23/2025. Received by fax 9/29.

CC: fever x2 days, RUQ abdominal pain.

HPI: 67M with COPD, HTN, hyperlipidemia. Two days of fevers at home and steady pain under the right ribs. No prior gallbladder trouble.

Meds: tiotropium, fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol prn, lisinopril 10, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81. Allergy: sulfa (rash). Former smoker, quit 2023.

Exam: uncomfortable, grimaces and tender when the right upper quadrant is pressed. Lungs without wheeze. Heart regular.

Labs: WBC 15.0, Hgb 12.2, plt 250. AST 80, ALT 75, alk phos 200, T bili 1.8, D bili 1.2.
RUQ US: distended gallbladder, thick wall, pericholecystic fluid, no stones.

Impression: acute acalculous cholecystitis. IV antibiotics started, surgery paged. Admitted to medicine.

medications.drug: amoxicillin 875 MG / clavulanate 125 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with food for 7 days

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, medicine service. Admitted 9/23/2025, discharged 9/26/2025.

Diagnosis: acute acalculous cholecystitis.

Course: Admitted from the ED with fever, RUQ tenderness and leukocytosis; ultrasound with a distended, thick-walled gallbladder, pericholecystic fluid and no stones. Treated with IV antibiotics and bowel rest, then diet. General surgery saw him on admission and recommended nonoperative management given his COPD; no interval cholecystectomy planned unless symptoms return. Fever resolved within a day, pain improved steadily, eating by day 2.

Discharge medications: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily for 7 more days (new). Continue tiotropium, fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol as needed, lisinopril 10 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg.
Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).

Follow-up: PCP within 1 to 2 weeks with CBC and liver tests. Return for fever, worsening pain, jaundice or vomiting.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt after hospital discharge for gallbladder infection. Home since Friday. No fever since leaving. Soreness under the right ribs much better, eating light. Taking the antibiotic twice a day with food, no problems with it. Breathing at baseline. Reviewed reasons to go back to the ED. Appointment made Thursday with PCP, labs that day.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after 3-night admission 9/23-9/26 for acute acalculous cholecystitis, treated with antibiotics, no surgery. Discharge summary and ED record reviewed.

Now: no fevers, appetite back, only a faint ache under the right ribs if he presses there. Two more days of amoxicillin-clavulanate. Breathing unchanged from baseline, no extra albuterol use in the hospital or since.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Not jaundiced. Abdomen soft, very mild RUQ tenderness, no guarding, negative Murphy. Lungs as usual, diminished, no wheeze.

A/P
Acute acalculous cholecystitis, improving. Finish antibiotic. CBC and liver panel today to make sure the counts and bilirubin have come back down. Surgery's plan is no operation unless it recurs; reviewed what a recurrence would feel like.
COPD, HTN stable. Keep the October 24 visit for flu shot and COVID.

documents.title: Follow-up labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: White count and liver tests are all back to normal. Exactly what we wanted to see after the gallbladder infection. See you on the 24th.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back to himself after the September gallbladder episode. No RUQ pain since finishing the antibiotic, eating everything. Breathing about the same as the spring, albuterol a few times a week now that it is colder. No sputum change, no fevers.
Meds reviewed, unchanged: tiotropium daily, fluticasone/salmeterol bid, albuterol prn, lisinopril 10, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81.

O: vitals as charted. Abdomen soft, nontender. Lungs diminished at bases, no wheeze or crackles. Heart regular.

A/P
1. Acute acalculous cholecystitis, resolved. Labs normalized 10/2.
2. COPD, stable. Continue current inhalers.
3. HTN controlled.
4. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin, lipids due at the January visit.
5. Flu (high-dose) and COVID given.
RTC January, fasting labs then. Lung CT due January as well.

documents.title: Cancelled Appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel tomorrow's 3-month follow-up, roads are bad out his way and he'd rather not drive in it. Says he feels fine. Offered February dates, he will call back once he checks his calendar.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic requests from his pharmacy for lisinopril 10 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg, 90 days. Last BP in October controlled, last labs normal. Approved by PCP x1 with a note on the bottle to book his overdue follow-up.

documents.title: ICU Admission Note
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital medical ICU. Date of service 3/20/2026. Received with the discharge packet 5/29.

Reason for admission: acute hypoxemic respiratory failure.

68-year-old man with COPD (GOLD Group C), hypertension and hyperlipidemia, seen in this hospital's ED about six months ago for acute cholecystitis. Brought in with worsening shortness of breath and low oxygen; intubated in the ED and moved to the ICU on mechanical ventilation.

Home medications: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 twice daily, albuterol as needed, lisinopril 10 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg. Allergy: sulfa drugs (rash). Former smoker, 48 pack-years, quit 2023. Social alcohol.

Ventilator: volume control, tidal volume 450 mL, rate 16, FiO2 60%, PEEP 5 cm H2O. SpO2 only 88% on these settings.
Exam: sedated on the ventilator. Crackles in both lungs, breath sounds decreased at both bases. Heart regular. No leg edema.
ABG on FiO2 0.60: pH 7.32, PaCO2 50, PaO2 58, HCO3 24.
Chest film: bilateral infiltrates consistent with ARDS.

Assessment: ARDS with refractory hypoxemia on underlying COPD.
Plan: low tidal volume ventilation, PEEP titration upward, prone positioning if oxygenation does not improve, sedation, ICU care.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 3/20/2026, discharged 5/27/2026 to an inpatient rehabilitation facility.

Diagnoses: acute respiratory distress syndrome with refractory hypoxemia; acute hypoxic respiratory failure; prolonged mechanical ventilation; acute acalculous cholecystitis (4/28), treated with percutaneous cholecystostomy. Chronic: COPD, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.

Course:
Respiratory. Intubated on arrival for hypoxemia, SpO2 88% on FiO2 60% and PEEP 5. ABG pH 7.32 / PaCO2 50 / PaO2 58 / HCO3 24. Bilateral infiltrates on chest film. Managed with lung-protective ventilation, PEEP titrated up, and several prone positioning sessions for refractory hypoxemia. A specific precipitant was not established. Oxygenation improved slowly, but he could not be weaned, and a tracheostomy was placed 4/3. Liberated from the ventilator 5/11. Decannulated 5/19, stoma covered and healing.
Biliary. On ICU day 40 (4/28) he developed fever, leukocytosis and new RUQ tenderness. Ultrasound showed a thick-walled gallbladder with pericholecystic fluid and no stones. General surgery consulted; interventional radiology placed a percutaneous cholecystostomy drain 4/29, and IV antibiotics were given. Fever resolved within two days. Drain remains in place at discharge, to be studied by IR in about 6 weeks.

Discharge medications: home regimen resumed unchanged: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 twice daily, albuterol as needed, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).

Follow-up: interventional radiology drain check in about 6 weeks; primary care after rehab discharge.

documents.title: Call from Hospital Case Manager
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ICU case manager from the regional hospital called to let us know pt was admitted 3/20 with respiratory failure, on a ventilator in the ICU. Asked for his medication list and recent notes, faxed. They will send records at discharge. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: RE: Call from Hospital Case Manager
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Noted. Please flag the chart so we catch the discharge summary and set up a hospital follow-up when he's out.

events.reason: Fever and new right upper quadrant pain in the ICU

reports.text: Portable bedside study in the ICU. Indication: fever, leukocytosis, right upper quadrant pain. Gallbladder wall is thickened with pericholecystic fluid. No gallstones. Common bile duct normal in caliber. Liver normal in echotexture without focal lesion.
reports.conclusion: Thickened gallbladder wall with pericholecystic fluid, no gallstones; acalculous cholecystitis.

procedures.procedure: Percutaneous cholecystostomy and drainage using ultrasound guidance

documents.title: General Surgery Consultation
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital general surgery, inpatient consult in the medical ICU, 4/28/2026. Received with the discharge packet.

Asked to see for fever and RUQ pain. 68M, ICU day 40 for ARDS, trached and on the ventilator. Over the last 24 hours temperature to 38.9, rising white count, new pain on RUQ exam. Had an episode of acalculous cholecystitis last September managed without surgery.

Exam: sedated on the ventilator. Grimaces with pressure over the right upper quadrant. Murphy sign can't be judged with sedation. Abdomen otherwise soft, not distended.
Labs: WBC 16.0, Hgb 13.2, plt 210. AST 70, ALT 65, alk phos 120, T bili 1.2. Lipase 22.
US: no stones, thick gallbladder wall, pericholecystic fluid.

Impression: acute acalculous cholecystitis in a critically ill ventilated patient. Not an operative candidate now.
Recommend: IV antibiotics; IR percutaneous cholecystostomy. We will follow.

Addendum 4/29: IR placed an ultrasound-guided cholecystostomy drain. Tolerated without complication.

documents.title: Inpatient Rehabilitation Discharge Summary
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
Inpatient rehabilitation facility, admitted 5/27/2026 from the regional hospital ICU, discharged home 6/17/2026.

Reason for admission: debility after a prolonged ICU stay for ARDS with tracheostomy (decannulated 5/19) and a percutaneous cholecystostomy drain for acalculous cholecystitis.

Course: daily physical and occupational therapy. Progressed from a walker to walking household and short community distances without a device. Stairs with one rail. Self-care independent by discharge. Trach stoma closed. Cholecystostomy drain flushed daily, output low and clear, no fevers. Breathing at rest comfortable on room air throughout.

Discharge medications: unchanged home regimen: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 twice daily, albuterol as needed, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: sulfa (rash).

Follow-up: IR drain check scheduled 7/8; PCP within 2 weeks; home exercise program.

documents.title: Home now
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got home from the rehab place yesterday. They said to see you in a couple weeks. Also need refills on the two inhalers, I'm down to a few days. Still have the tube in my side until the radiology appointment.

documents.title: RE: Home now
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Welcome home. You're booked with your doctor July 14 at 11:00. Refill request sent to the nurse.

documents.title: Inhaler Refills
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Tiotropium capsules and fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 refilled, 90 days, per PCP. Rehab summary reviewed, regimen unchanged from before admission. Pharmacy confirmed ready for pickup.

reports.text: Contrast injected through the existing cholecystostomy catheter. The gallbladder fills without filling defect. The cystic duct is patent and contrast flows into the common bile duct and on into the duodenum. No leak.

documents.title: Interventional Radiology Procedure Letter
documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Interventional radiology, regional hospital. Date of procedure 7/8/2026.

Drain study through the percutaneous cholecystostomy placed 4/29. Patient has felt well, no fevers or right-sided pain since rehab. Cholangiogram: cystic duct open, free flow into the duodenum, no leak. Catheter removed intact; dry dressing on the site. Keep it covered for 48 hours. Call for fever, pain or drainage from the site.

Allergies: sulfa (rash). No change to his medications.

documents.title: Cancelled Appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel tomorrow, his ride fell through and he is not driving yet after the hospital stay. Doing ok otherwise. Asked him to call back with a date when he has transportation; gave him the number for the senior van.

documents.title: Rescheduling
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sorry about missing last month. Radiology took the tube out and I'm getting around better. Can we pick a day in early September, mornings are best.

documents.title: RE: Rescheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Booked for Thursday, September 3 at 9:20 with your doctor. We'll send a reminder the day before.
